source: Quiz 2 - Sessions 1-3: Choosing a Model and Thinking Budgets
question: Fable was not released as soon as it was ready. What reason did the lecture give?

options.text: It proved unusually good at hacking.
options.feedback: Along with solving hard problems and working for long stretches, that capability came with the size. It is why a model being ready did not by itself mean a model being released.

options.text: It generated tokens more slowly than the tier below it.
options.feedback: It certainly is not quick, but slowness is the expected cost of size and is true of every tier above the smallest, so it would not single Fable out. The hold-up was something the model could do, not something it was slow at.

options.text: It could not use the same tools the smaller tiers use.
options.feedback: Tooling is broadly shared across tiers, so a gap there is not the sort of thing that delays a release. The concern was what the model was unusually good at, not what it lacked.

options.text: Its answers were less accurate than the tier below it.
options.feedback: Fable was described as having capabilities not seen in earlier models, so weak answers were not the problem. Some of those new capabilities were the problem.
